changes: Persons, relations and date kept as they were; only the notes are expanded
Notes now say that Hīra and Māmalladevī are the author's parents, from the stock end-of-canto verse, and have nothing to do with this copy
Notes now say the poet is usually called Śrīharṣa; 'Harṣa' is kept because the rule strips śrī
Notes now say the era NS is only inferred from 'nepālīya'; no year, scribe or place can be read

notes: The scribe's part of the colophon starts after 'nepālīya' and runs two more lines, which the cataloguer could not read on the microfilm (perhaps lighter ink). They may still be legible on the original manuscript. The era NS is inferred from 'nepālīya [saṃvat]'. No year, scribe, commissioner or place survives. The persons are taken only from the author's stock end-of-canto verse: Śrīharṣa (written 'Harṣa' here, without śrī, as the rule requires; he is usually known as Śrīharṣa), his father Hīra and his mother Māmalladevī. None of them is connected with the making of this copy. The text has the usual errors: 'naiṣadhīyarite', 'nosarggojvalaḥ', 'naiṣada'.
